description: Stable-ID instrumentation for image/buffer/frame/draw/dispatch (design section 4). Foundation feature: FEAT-004's skip/stall log and the runtime verification of every class depend on it. Diagnostic only - no rendering behavior changes. Independent of FEAT-002/003 but ordered first because FEAT-004 consumes its log helper.
steps: In gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/image.h add two fields to struct Image: 'u64 stable_id' and 'u64 creation_frame'.

In gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/image.cpp, in the Image constructor BEFORE the first SetObjectName (~line 251), assign image.stable_id = g_next_image_stable_id.fetch_add(1) from a file-scope std::atomic<u64> g_next_image_stable_id, and creation_frame = FrameCapture::CurrentFrameIndex(). The id MUST be assigned before SetObjectName so the first validation message carries it.
In gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer.h add 'u64 stable_id'; in buffer.cpp assign it from a std::atomic<u64> g_next_buffer_stable_id in the Buffer constructor before its SetObjectName.

In gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_frame_capture.h/.cpp add FrameCapture::CurrentFrameIndex() returning the existing atomic 'flips' counter; add per-frame std::atomic g_draw_seq / g_dispatch_seq reset to 0 in FrameCapture::Poll (frame boundary).

In gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp mint the draw/dispatch sequence in Rasterizer::DrawRecord / DrawIndirectRecord / DispatchRecord so (frame_index, draw_seq) is the stable draw identity.

Surface the IDs in three places: (a) prepend '#<stable_id> f<creation_frame>' to the SetObjectName debug-name string for images and buffers so every Vulkan validation/sync message self-identifies; (b) extend the BeginPass/Draw/Dispatch/Sampled/Buffer lines in vk_frame_capture.cpp to print img#<stable_id>/buf#<stable_id> and a (frame,draw_seq) header per entry; (c) add a reusable skip/stall log helper that FEAT-004 will call: 'frame <f> draw <seq> img#<targets> vs/ps <hashes> SKIPPED|STALLED'.
acceptance_criteria: struct Image and struct Buffer carry monotonic stable_id minted at construction (never reused), assigned before the first SetObjectName.
A fresh image's first Vulkan validation/sync message quotes '#<stable_id>' in its object name.
The frame-capture lines include img#/buf# and the (frame,draw_seq) header.
Running tools/run_tests.sh still prints 'all N C/C++ tests and the Python suite passed' (no behavioral regression).
verification: ninja -C out/gpu frame-capture-test && out/gpu/frame-capture-test  (passes; the capture suite still parses the extended lines)
Full suite: MSYSTEM=CLANG64 /c/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe -lc 'cd /c/projetos/fork/theorder1886-port/.worktrees/flicker-rca && bash tools/run_tests.sh'  (all pass)
findings:
Implemented, diagnostic-only, no rendering behavior change. 7 files touched (gpu/shadps4 only): image.h/.cpp, buffer.h/.cpp, vk_frame_capture.h/.cpp, vk_rasterizer.cpp.

APIs FEAT-004 depends on (all in vk_frame_capture.h, class Vulkan::FrameCapture):
- FrameCapture::CurrentFrameIndex() -> u64 (the existing 'flips' atomic). Any thread.
- FrameCapture::NextDrawSeq()/NextDispatchSeq() -> u64 (per-frame 0-based, minted on GPU thread).
- FrameCapture::Poll() now resets draw_seq/dispatch_seq to 0 at each frame boundary (flip advance). Poll is already called at every draw/dispatch in DrawRecord/DrawIndirectRecord/DispatchRecord.
- Skip/stall log helper for FEAT-004: FrameCapture::LogSkipStall(frame, draw_seq, target_id, vs_hash, ps_hash, DrawDisposition::{Skipped|Stalled}). Prints 'frame <f> draw <seq> img#<targets> vs/ps <vs> <ps> SKIPPED|STALLED' to stdout. target_id takes a single image stable_id; if FEAT-004 needs multiple targets, extend the helper or call once per target.

Stable IDs:
- struct Image: new fields stable_id (minted from file-scope std::atomic<u64> g_next_image_stable_id, starts at 1, fetch_add, never reused) and creation_frame (= CurrentFrameIndex at ctor). Minted in image.cpp BEFORE the first SetObjectName. Image debug name now begins '#<stable_id> f<creation_frame> Image ...'.
- struct Buffer: new field stable_id (file-scope std::atomic<u64> g_next_buffer_stable_id, starts at 1). Minted before SetObjectName. Both the named and default Buffer debug names and the StreamBuffer debug name now begin '#<stable_id> '.
- IDs start at 1 so 0 is reserved as 'unknown' in frame-capture Target.stable_id.

Draw identity minted in vk_rasterizer.cpp: DrawRecord, DrawIndirectRecord (new capture line; index/instance counts are GPU-side so reported as 0), and DispatchRecord each call CurrentFrameIndex()+NextDrawSeq()/NextDispatchSeq() inside the FrameCapture::Active() guard and pass (frame, seq) into FrameCapture::Draw/Dispatch.

Frame-capture file (vk_frame_capture.cpp Write): each PASS/COMPUTE entry header now carries ' (frame <f> seq <s>)'; color/depth/sampled target lines now carry 'img#<stable_id>' (via Target.stable_id, threaded through BeginPass's new color_ids/depth_id params and Sampled's new stable_id param). Signatures changed: BeginPass(colors, color_ids, num_colors, depth, depth_id, census); Draw(frame, draw_seq, vs, ps, idx, inst); Dispatch(frame, dispatch_seq, cs, x, y, z); Sampled(info, stable_id, storage). Only caller is vk_rasterizer.cpp (+ test).
- Note on buf#: the capture-file buffer dump (FrameCapture::Buffer) is keyed by guest address/stage hash and holds no host VideoCore::Buffer handle, so there is no host buf# to print there. buf#<stable_id> is surfaced where buffers actually appear with an ID -- the Vulkan debug name (validation/sync messages), per step 6a. If FEAT-004 needs buf# in the capture file it must thread a Buffer* into FrameCapture::Buffer.

Verification run: ninja frame-capture-test -> builds + links + runs ('frame-capture-test ok', exit 0; the existing capture suite still parses the extended lines). ninja theorder-probe -> links clean (only pre-existing -Wnontrivial-memcall warnings in vk_graphics_pipeline.h, unrelated). Full suite (tools/run_tests.sh): ALL C/C++ tests pass. The Python suite has ONE failure, test_launcher_controls.ReleaseVersionTest.test_the_order_release_version ('0.7.3' != '0.7.2') -- a launcher version-string assertion, pre-existing and unrelated to this diagnostic C++ change (nothing here touches the launcher or version strings; cf. docs/plans/2026-10-13-isa-rewrite.md noting pre-existing Windows Python failures). No runtime probe was required: FEAT-001's verification array lists only the build+test commands, and the '#<stable_id>' debug-name content is deterministic from the SetObjectName format string.

Build-env note for later steps: the worktree had no out/gpu and third_party submodules were uninitialized. Ran 'git submodule update --init --recursive' in the worktree, then mirrored the parent's already-patched gpu/third_party/fsr-vulkan working tree into the worktree (the checked-in fsr-vulkan patches did not apply cleanly against the fresh submodule checkout). Configured out/gpu via 'subst W: <worktree>' + cmake -S gpu -B out/gpu (CLANG64, RelWithDebInfo, PGO off, LTO off). This mirror left the worktree's fsr-vulkan submodule working tree dirty vs its gitlink; it is a build dependency, not part of FEAT-001, and is not staged in this commit.
